title: The Jackie Gleason tour with Joe Bushkin and Buck Clayton
summary: Jones and Hinton recall a five-to-six-week tour with Jackie Gleason's show and jazz stars, with a barbecue in Detroit and Gleason's generosity.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Fess is Cab Calloway. So after that where did you go? Now we're up to the 60's. We made a tour, by the way; we forgot to mention that.
When we did the 5 or 6 weeks with the Jackie Gleason show with Joe Bushkin, you, Buck Clayton, and myself, and Zuma Cunningham who was responsible for taking Mr. Clark Gable to Hollywood.
A great lady and a good actress.
The first one, when he did The Honeymooners -
The lady who tried the shoes on.
We went through all that and we had the DeMarco Sisters, and there was Art Carney.
That was a great tour, wasn't it?

Of course it was. That's when I found out that Jackie Gleason was the Fatty Arbuckle of his time because - he was a well-read man and he had the children. But this particular tour that we did was very remarkable. Now we go back after that -
How long was that tour, Jo?
JONES
The tour lasted 5½ or 6 weeks.
Let's name some of the towns. We went first to Pittsburgh.
Pittsburgh; we went to Detroit. We played Chicago at the Chicago Theatre.
Youngstown, Akron, Cincinnati -
We played Cincinnati. We played all of them.
Boston. I think the tour closed in Boston.

We closed in Boston because at the time, I think it was June or July, because I have a record that when I came into the Birdland with Tony Bennett and some more peoples and I was supposed to play with Basie's band at that particular time, I sat in the audience and I did not play in the band because I had to leave.
We had such a ball! The DeMarco Sisters - what was that guy's name, Stan something, a very funny guy -

A comedian that did all the parts. Then you remember that Jackie would always say, "Milt, didn't you fix the coffee?" and if he didn't get that coffee, that was it. Jackie at that particular time had a weight problem.
He contributed a great deal to jazz, didn't he?
One of the great supporters of jazz.

Oh, please. You remember the thing we did in Detroit? I went out and got Tommy Gamble - that's when we got Ahmad Jamal to come into the Embassy. There was about a party of 23 was down there. Jackie had the Presidential Suite at the Book-Cadillac. We said, well, we'll just go
JONES 202
around the corner and get some barbecue. Jackie said, "I've got $300 worth of barbecue! And his weight went up and naturally when we went to....
Tommy Gamble's house. He was one of the great sportsmen of Detroit, Tommy Gamble. Jackie was such a great supporter of jazz, wasn't he?

Yes. After that Jackie had the trumpet player that we all know so well to sit down just to make one record just for personal people and he only wanted to send this record out. Do you remember when we went to the Parke-Sheraton and Jackie was in the deep freeze, talking about he had to sober up. He put everything out of there. We were upstairs trying to figure out what we were going to play on the show. Buck had gone somewhere, and he did "Bob-a-loo" and he got Bobbie and he only did this record just for a few friends. Because, as I said, you know we know that he's well read, but out of that we did a thing. But at the time, you must remember, Milt, that you, Buck, Joe Bushkin, or myself were in demand and everybody was pulling on us. They didn't allow us the chance to be, to do what we wanted to do. However, out of that we did a lot of things.
